deep.reconstruction:
This page is the table of contents of a manuscript titled 'Structures stratifiées', with four sections and page numbers:

1. 'La situation type – préliminaires d'un programme' (p. 1): a motivating model situation and the outline of a research programme.
2. 'Stratifications globales : le formalisme ½ simplicial (sans tubes)' (p. 10): a combinatorial or (semi/symmetric-)simplicial description of a globally stratified object, without tubular neighbourhoods.
3. 'Introduction des tubes' (p. 16): adding tubular neighbourhoods, the 'tubes' of Esquisse d'un programme §5.
4. 'Topos canoniques associés à une stratification (globale)' (p. 23): attaching a canonical topos to a stratified object.

The next page already starts the section-2 combinatorics. It works with a truncated diagram E0 ⇇ E1 ⇇ E2 carrying actions of S2 on E1 and S3 on E2. It writes out the face maps (p_ij) and degeneracy-type maps (δ_i) with relations, i.e. a 2-truncated symmetric (semi-)simplicial set: equivalence-relation or groupoid-like data. Grothendieck then reduces this to minimal generators p0, p12, δ0, δ1 plus symmetry relations.

In modern terms the programme is roughly as follows. Describe a stratified space or scheme by:
- its strata;
- the incidence relations between strata, organised simplicially by chains of strata;
- then the tubular data (link or tube fibrations between strata, the 'dévissage' of Esquisse §5);
- finally a topos encoding the whole stratified homotopy type.
The closest modern analogue of that topos is the exit-path category or ∞-category and its constructible-sheaf topos (MacPherson; Treumann; Lurie HA App. A; Barwick–Glasman–Haine 'Exodromy'). The problem served is a 'tame topology' foundation for stratified structures, as announced in Esquisse §§5–6.

ideas.what: Programme of a theory of stratified structures, organised as global stratification combinatorics, then tubes, then canonical topos
ideas.modern_name: Tame topology / stratified spaces with tubular data (Mather–Thom control data); stratified homotopy theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather (control data); Grothendieck announced the programme in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §§5–6 (topologie modérée, théorème de dévissage des structures stratifiées)

ideas.what: Combinatorial '½ simplicial' formalism for global stratifications without tubes
ideas.modern_name: Stratification as a functor to a poset / simplicial (or symmetric semi-simplicial) incidence data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Various; poset-stratified spaces formalised by Lurie (HA App. A)

ideas.what: Canonical topos associated to a (global) stratification
ideas.modern_name: Topos of constructible sheaves / exit-path category; exodromy
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths, unpublished), Treumann 2009, Lurie, Barwick–Glasman–Haine 2018+
ideas.where_published: Esquisse hints at stratified homotopy types, but not, to my knowledge, explicitly at a canonical stratified topos

deep.surprise_reason: This is only a table of contents. It confirms a planned treatment of stratified structures with tubes and an associated canonical topos, consistent with Esquisse d'un programme. The section on canonical topoi is suggestive, but no mathematics is shown here.
